questions.question_text:
An electricity bill lists the last account as $\$247.00$ and the current total amount due as $\$312.00$.
By how much has the bill increased?

options.why: Takes the current total amount due instead of subtracting the last account.
Borrows a ten for the units column but fails to reduce the tens column when subtracting $312 - 247$.
Adds the current bill and the last account instead of subtracting.

questions.question_text:
An electricity bill lists: current charges excluding GST $\$372.00$; GST $\$37.20$; total amount due including GST $\$409.20$.
How much GST was charged?

options.why: Reads the current charges excluding GST instead of the GST amount.
Reads the total amount due including GST instead of the GST amount.
Calculates $10\%$ of the GST-inclusive total of $\$409.20$ instead of reading the stated GST.

questions.solution_text: The bill states that GST of $\$37.20$ was charged.

questions.question_text:
A residential water bill lists: water usage charge $\$142.80$; total service charges $\$204.60$; total current charges $\$347.40$.
It states that GST does not apply to usage or service charges.
How much GST was charged?

options.why: Calculates $10\%$ of the total current charges of $\$347.40$ despite the statement that GST does not apply.
Incorrectly charges $10\%$ GST on the water usage charge of $\$142.80$.
Incorrectly charges $10\%$ GST on the service charges of $\$204.60$.

questions.solution_text: GST does not apply to the listed charges, so the GST charged is $\$0.00$.

questions.question_text:
A water bill covers $1$ July to $30$ September. The homeowner refilled their pool on $8$ October. The bill was issued on $12$ October and is due on $26$ October.
Is the pool refill included in this bill?

options.text: No, the refill occurred after the billing period ended on $30$ September.
Yes, the refill occurred before the issue date of $12$ October.
options.why: Uses the issue date as the end of the usage period instead of $30$ September.

options.text: Yes, the refill occurred before the due date of $26$ October.
options.why: Uses the payment due date as the end of the usage period.

options.text: Yes, all October water use is included because the bill was issued in October.
options.why: Uses the month of issue instead of the stated July-to-September billing period.

questions.solution_text: No. The refill on $8$ October occurred after the billing period ended on $30$ September.

questions.question_text:
A monthly telecommunications bundle increased in price from $\$75.00$ to $\$84.00$.
What is the percentage increase? Round to two decimal places where appropriate.

options.why: Confuses the dollar increase of $\$9.00$ with a percentage.
Divides the $\$9$ increase by the new amount $\$84$ instead of the original $\$75$.
Calculates the ratio of new to old bill without subtracting $100\%$.

questions.question_text:
A quarterly electricity bill lists a total energy consumption of $1820\text{ kWh}$ across a $91$-day billing cycle.
What was the average daily electricity consumption? Round to two decimal places where appropriate.

options.why: Divides by $100$ instead of the actual billing duration of $91$ days.
Divides by $11$ instead of $91$ days.
Divides by $30$ days assuming a standard month instead of $91$ days.

questions.question_text:
An electricity bill lists the last account as $\$328.40$ and the current total amount due as $\$369.45$.
Express the increase as a percentage of the last bill, correct to two decimal places.

options.why: Divides the increase of $\$41.05$ by the current bill of $\$369.45$ instead of the last bill of $\$328.40$.
Treats the dollar increase of $\$41.05$ as the percentage increase.
Divides the current bill by the last bill and multiplies by $100\%$ without subtracting $100\%$.

questions.question_text:
A three-person household on a $620\text{ m}^2$ property used $43.2\text{ kL}$ of water over $90$ days.
For three-person households, the targets are: small property, $463\text{ L/day}$; medium property, $477\text{ L/day}$; large property, $498\text{ L/day}$. A medium property has an area between $501\text{ m}^2$ and $700\text{ m}^2$.
Which statement correctly compares the household's daily water use with its target? Use $1\text{ kL} = 1000\text{ L}$.

options.text: They used $480\text{ L/day}$, exceeding their target of $477\text{ L/day}$ by $3\text{ L/day}$.
They used $480\text{ L/day}$, meeting a target of $498\text{ L/day}$.
options.why: Selects the large-property target instead of the medium-property target for an area of $620\text{ m}^2$.

options.text: They used $160\text{ L/day}$, meeting their household target of $477\text{ L/day}$.
options.why: Divides the household daily usage by the three occupants and compares per-person usage with a whole-household target.

options.text: They used $0.48\text{ L/day}$, meeting their target of $477\text{ L/day}$.
options.why: Divides $43.2$ by $90$ without converting kilolitres to litres, then labels the result as litres per day.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Total litres} = 43.2 \times 1000 = 43\,200\text{ L}$
$\text{Household daily usage} = \dfrac{43\,200}{90} = 480\text{ L/day}$
The property is medium-sized, so the target for three occupants is $477\text{ L/day}$.
$\text{Amount above target} = 480 - 477 = 3\text{ L/day}$
The household is not meeting its target.
